summary: Nikolai Anderson was a linguist who studied at the University of Tartu under Leo Meyer. He served as Oberlehrer für alte Sprachen at Minsk Gymnasium (1872–1894) and Eo. Professor of Finno-Ugric at Kazan State University (1894–1905).

Nikolai Maksimovich Goldberg was an indologist and historian who studied at Heidelberg University (1910–1912). He held posts at the Institute of History (1938) and the Institute of Oriental Studies (1943) of the Soviet Academy of Sciences.

Nikolai Solmsdorf specializes in tibetology and buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Munich under Franz-Karl Ehrhard and Alexander von Rospatt, and held a post at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2013).

Nikolai Trubetzkoy studied linguistics at Moscow State University under Wiktor Porzeziński and at Leipzig under Leskien, Brugmann, Sievers, and Windisch. He taught at Moscow, Southern Federal University, Sofia University, and as Professor of Slavic at Vienna (1922).

Nikolaj Dmitrievič Andreev was a computational linguist and indologist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University. He worked at the Leningrad State University Experimental Laboratory of Machine Translation (1959–1965) and the Institute for Linguistic Studies (~1956–1986).

Nikolaus Delius studied linguistics and indology at Berlin under Franz Bopp and at Bonn under A. W. von Schlegel and Christian Lassen. He was a Privatdozent in Berlin and later Professor of English at Bonn (1855–1880).

Nikolay Astakhaev, active in buddhist studies, sinology, and philosophy, studied at Buryat State University (2005–2008). He later worked at the Irkutsk Institute of Educators Training (2012–2015) and at Yandex's Novosibirsk office (2015).

Nikolay Ivanovich Korolev was an indologist and linguist who studied at Moscow State University's Institute of Asian and African Studies (~1953–1958). In 1958, he became a research scholar at the Institute of Oriental Studies.

Linguist Nils Holmer studied at Lund University and Charles University. He served as Privatdozent of Celtic and Indo-European at Uppsala University (1941) and as Professor of Linguistics at Lund University (1949–1969).

Nils Olof Mathias Flensburg was a linguist and indologist who completed his education at Lund University. He taught at Lunds privata elementarskola (1887–1919) and served as Professor of Sanskrit and comparative Indo-European linguistics at Lund University (1898–1920).

Nils Simonsson studied indology and tibetology at Uppsala, Oslo, and Paris under Helmer Smith, Georg Morgenstierne, Louis Renou, and Marcelle Lalou. He was Professor of Indian languages and literature at Oslo (1963–1975) and at Uppsala (1976–1985).
Nima Repper is an indologist who is attested in 2026 as a Wissenschaftliche Mitarbeiterin at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Nimethri Gunasekara is active in buddhist studies. She served as a Visiting Lecturer at the University of Kelaniya in 2024 and at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies as a psychologist, mindfulness trainer, and lecturer (attested 2026).

Nina Mirnig, a scholar of indology and religious studies, completed her doctorate under Alexis Sanderson. She has held positions at the University of Groningen, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, and serves as Deputy Head at the University of Vienna.

Ninian Smart was a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and indology who studied at Oxford and Yale. He held professorships at the University of Birmingham, Lancaster University (1967–1989), and the University of California, Santa Barbara (1976–1998).

Historian and indologist Nira Wickramasinghe studied at Paris-Sorbonne University and the University of Oxford. She served as Professor of History and International Relations at the University of Colombo (1990–2009) and became Chair of Modern South Asian Studies at Leiden University (2010).

Indologist Nirajan Kafle earned his doctorate at Leiden University under Peter C. Bisschop. He has held positions at the Nepal Research Centre, Leiden University, the University of Naples "L'Orientale", and taught Sanskrit at Ashoka University starting in 2023.

Niranjan Prasad Chakravarti, an indologist and historian, studied at Calcutta, Cambridge (under E. J. Rapson), Paris, and Berlin. He served as Government Epigraphist and as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1948–1950).

Nirbhay N. Singh has held posts as Professor of Psychiatry, Pediatrics, and Psychology at Virginia Commonwealth University, Director of the Commonwealth Institute for Family Studies, and Clinical Professor of Psychiatry and Health Behavior at Augusta University (attested 2015–2018).
Nirmal C. Sinha served as the editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology, attested in 1978 and 1988.
